edit_summary: When a memory-backed WAV write needs more than the doubled capacity, grow to the incoming chunk length instead of current position plus chunk length.
root_cause: The fallback capacity calculation must be relative to the current write cursor, not just the size of the current write.
effect_path: After earlier writes move currentWritePos near the end of the memory stream, a large metadata or audio write reallocates a buffer that is smaller than currentWritePos + bytesToWrite and the following DRWAV_COPY_MEMORY writes past it.
guard_p1: A memory write stream has existing contents and currentWritePos is nonzero near the current capacity.
guard_p2: The next write is larger than the remaining space and also larger than the doubled-capacity slack, such as a large metadata chunk or PCM frame batch.
hardness_reason: The under-allocation depends on persistent memory-stream state accumulated by previous writes before the growth branch is reached.
naturalness_reason: Dropping the cursor component from a relative growth calculation is a plausible dynamic-buffer bug.
explanation: The fallback capacity calculation must be relative to the current write cursor, not just the size of the current write. After earlier writes move currentWritePos near the end of the memory stream, a large metadata or audio write reallocates a buffer that is smaller than currentWritePos + bytesToWrite and the following DRWAV_COPY_MEMORY writes past it.

edit_summary: Leave the metadata buffer attached to the drwav object after returning it to the caller.
root_cause: Taking ownership of parsed metadata must detach the buffer from the live drwav object.
effect_path: A caller that takes metadata ownership keeps the returned allocation, then drwav_uninit later follows the still-populated pWav->pMetadata field and frees the same allocation before the caller releases it.
guard_p1: A RIFF/RF64 input is opened with DRWAV_WITH_METADATA and produces at least one metadata record.
guard_p2: The caller uses drwav_take_ownership_of_metadata before drwav_uninit and then frees the returned metadata as documented.
hardness_reason: The first ownership transfer and the later library teardown are separated by an API boundary and caller-controlled lifetime, so the duplicated owner is not visible as an adjacent free pair.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to clear ownership state after a take-ownership API is a realistic lifetime regression.
explanation: Taking ownership of parsed metadata must detach the buffer from the live drwav object. A caller that takes metadata ownership keeps the returned allocation, then drwav_uninit later follows the still-populated pWav->pMetadata field and frees the same allocation before the caller releases it.
first_free_site_expected: drwav_uninit frees pWav->pMetadata on the read-mode teardown path
second_free_site_expected: caller frees the metadata pointer returned by drwav_take_ownership_of_metadata
conditional_expected: Positive uses metadata parsing plus take-ownership before uninit; negative either does not parse metadata or lets drwav_uninit retain sole ownership.

root_cause: The compressed WAV decoders have fixed two-channel state arrays but initialization must reject larger channel counts.
effect_path: After the malformed format chunk is accepted, drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__ima or drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__msadpcm iterates iChannel or predictor slots using pWav->channels and indexes past the two-element decoder state.
guard_p1: The fmt/COMM chunk declares ADPCM or DVI ADPCM with exactly three channels and otherwise valid block alignment.
guard_p2: A normal read API is called after successful initialization so the compressed decoder consumes the first audio block.
hardness_reason: The bad channel count is accepted during container initialization, while the memory effect appears later in a codec-specific read path selected through translatedFormatTag.
naturalness_reason: Loosening a format support limit without widening the codec state is a plausible compatibility regression.
explanation: The compressed WAV decoders have fixed two-channel state arrays but initialization must reject larger channel counts. After the malformed format chunk is accepted, drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__ima or drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__msadpcm iterates iChannel or predictor slots using pWav->channels and indexes past the two-element decoder state.
boundary_invariant: Compressed decoder state in drwav.msadpcm and drwav.ima is sized for at most two channels.
neighbor_case: The same compressed stream with channels == 2 stays within predictor and cached-frame arrays.
oob_site_expected: drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__ima iChannel-indexed predictor/stepIndex access or drwav_read_pcm_frames_s16__msadpcm predictor access.

edit_summary: Stop reserving worst-case padding for aligned metadata payloads during the counting pass.
root_cause: The first metadata pass must include possible alignment padding because the second pass advances pDataCursor before aligned cue and sampler arrays.
effect_path: A preceding odd-sized metadata string or unknown chunk leaves pDataCursor misaligned; the read pass then aligns the cursor and writes a full cue point or sampler-loop array into a buffer whose counted capacity omitted that padding.
guard_p1: Metadata parsing is enabled and an odd-sized LIST/unknown payload precedes a cue or smpl metadata chunk that requests DRWAV_METADATA_ALIGNMENT.
guard_p2: The second metadata pass allocates the exact counted capacity and then calls drwav__metadata_get_memory for the aligned array.
hardness_reason: The count pass, allocation, cursor alignment, and later metadata object population are separate phases, so the overflow is only exposed by a specific ordering of metadata chunks.
naturalness_reason: Forgetting to reserve alignment slack in a two-pass arena allocator is a realistic memory-accounting mistake.
explanation: The first metadata pass must include possible alignment padding because the second pass advances pDataCursor before aligned cue and sampler arrays. A preceding odd-sized metadata string or unknown chunk leaves pDataCursor misaligned; the read pass then aligns the cursor and writes a full cue point or sampler-loop array into a buffer whose counted capacity omitted that padding.
boundary_invariant: extraCapacity must cover both payload bytes and up to align - 1 bytes of cursor padding.
boundary_case: An odd-length metadata payload is followed by an aligned cue-point or sampler-loop allocation.
neighbor_case: The aligned chunk is first in the arena or follows an already aligned payload.
oob_site_expected: drwav__read_cue_to_metadata_obj writes pCuePoints or drwav__read_smpl_to_metadata_obj writes pLoops after pDataCursor alignment consumes unreserved bytes.
